subject: Post-call exec debrief: pain → outcome mapping and procurement path
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@medivance.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medivance.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T16:22:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap and next steps — mapping pain to outcomes

Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick written summary so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps for your execs. I focused this on the sponsor-level outcomes we discussed and the procurement path you signaled.

Key pain points (as we heard):
- Inefficient inference cost at peak usage (30–40% over budgeted ML infra) impacting product margin.
- Latency variability on customer-facing features (p99 spikes during batch night jobs).
- Lack of standardized rollout for model updates (manual ops work, inconsistent regressions).

Desired business outcomes (measurable):
- Reduce inference unit cost by 25% on typical workload mix (target: $0.012/token equivalent).
- Keep p99 latency for search/assistant below 250ms in production SLA window.
- Enable safe canary rollouts with automated fallback to avoid user-facing regressions.

Constraints and risks you flagged:
- Must preserve PHI boundaries — solution needs to run in your VPC or on dedicated capacity (no shared-tenancy data plane).
- Procurement requires a one-page SOW + SOC2 evidence and a short pilot before enterprise procurement sign-off.
- Budget window: Q2 budget review on 2027-05-03; procurement will want pilot results before that date.

Proposed pilot approach (lean, 6 weeks):
1) Week 0–1: Access + baseline capture (redwood dedicated or private staging in your VPC).
2) Week 2–4: Pilot traffic (10–20% of inference volume routed) focusing on the assistant flow and nightly batch runs.
3) Week 5: Quantified cost/latency delta + short eval on quality regressions tied to your prompt set.
4) Week 6: Exec readout and procurement packet (SOW + pricing bands + SOC2 evidence).

Immediate asks / owners:
- Alex: confirm exec sponsor (name and contact) and procurement POC.
- Procurement Team: send the vendor intake template or confirm preferred contract template.
- Karthik (cc): I asked him to scope a conservative pricing band for the pilot and draft a one-page SOW.

Attachments: MediVance-Discovery-Map.xlsx (call map + data footprint), MediVance-MAP-ROI-v1.pdf (initial ROI sketch).

Next steps (calendar):
- I will follow up with a draft one-page SOW + pilot pricing by Mon 2027-03-15.
- Please confirm sponsor and procurement POC by Fri 2027-03-19 so we can lock the pilot window.

Thanks again — looking forward to keeping momentum.

—
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@medivance.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medivance.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-13T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and next steps — mapping pain to outcomes

Priyom — thanks for the crisp note and the attachments. This matches my notes and will be helpful to show to our CTO and the head of platform. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- On "reduce inference unit cost by 25%": we mean token-equivalent cost across both short-chat and long-form generation paths, weighted about 70/30.
- PHI constraint is non-negotiable — we will need a deployment model that leaves logs and raw payloads inside our VPC.
- Procurement POC is Emma Foster (emma.foster@medivance.com). She will own the vendor intake and contracting timeline.

I'll introduce Emma and our CTO (Tom Wallace) on the thread early next week. For now, can you also share the standard SOC2 evidence package (stub OK for now) and a sample pilot SOW with SLAs?

On timing: the Q2 budget review is 2027-05-03 but internal execs may want a short walk-through the week prior — we'll confirm.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap and next steps — mapping pain to outcomes

Adding a procurement + risk lens from our side.

Pilot commercial framing (short):
- 6-week pilot priced as a time-and-materials + capped usage band. We propose a fixed pilot fee (covers dedicated staging and engineer time) + a per-token overage cap.
- If pilot meets the cost/latency targets, we convert to a 12-month committed Dedicated capacity agreement with month-to-month scaling.

Risk mitigations for execs:
- Data residency: Private deployment within MediVance VPC (we'll provide a Terraform module and onboarding runbook).
- Regressions: Baseline prompt set + automated A/B regression checks included in pilot scope.
- Uptime / fallback: Canary with automatic fallback to current model variant for 5xx/p95 anomalies.

Reqs from MediVance to unblock contracting:
1) Sponsor intro (CTO Tom Wallace) — to validate target metrics
2) Procurement intake form or template (Emma) — to align on PO vs. contract cadence
3) Confirmation of sample dataset for latency/cost baseline (if sharing, must be de-identified or within VPC)

Attached: SOC2-evidence-stub.zip (we can provide full pack once NDA/PO in-place). I'll draft the one-page SOW and pilot pricing; Priyom — can you review and we sync on Monday?

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0247

Short internal ask: Priyom/Karthik — please circulate a one-page exec brief that succinctly maps: 1) current pain -> 2) pilot approach -> 3) success metrics and 4) ask of the sponsor (CTO sign-off + procurement timeline). Keep it to one page we can hand to Tom and Emma.

Also include two pricing bands for the pilot (conservative / aggressive) and an estimated delta to expected run-rate post-commitment. I'll introduce Tom and Emma once we have the one-pager.

If you want, I can also pull a short slide (2 slides) for the walk-through next week.

Thanks — Marissa
